alt: Green phytoplankton and sediment-rich water off Mauritania's desert coast, observed by Aqua MODIS.
caption: Aqua MODIS, 5 May 2020. Upwelling in the Canary Current system supplies nutrients off Mauritania. The visible green water contains phytoplankton and sediment; it is not a temperature map.

credit: Robert Simmon / NASA Earth Observatory · Aqua MODIS / EOSDIS · public domain · resized
alt: Afternoon cumulus clouds over Sri Lanka, observed by Aqua MODIS on 9 April 2013.
caption: Aqua MODIS, 9 April 2013. Sea-breeze air moves inland and helps cumulus clouds develop over the warmer island. Silvery water is sunglint. This daytime image shows sea-breeze effects, not a night-time land breeze.

credit: Jesse Allen / NASA Earth Observatory · AMSR-E / Remote Sensing Systems · public domain · resized
alt: AMSR-E sea-surface temperature anomalies around northern Australia in the Indo-Pacific warm pool.
caption: AMSR-E, 19 October 2004. This warm-pool region was cooler than its long-term average. Colours show temperature anomalies, not absolute water temperature; a negative anomaly does not mean the water is cold in absolute terms.
